theme: Rest, memory verse, week-in-review (final partial week)
memoryText: For all the promises of God find their Yes in him. That is why it is through him that we utter our Amen to God for his glory.
readingInstruction: This is the last day of the plan. There is no new reading today. Read 2 Corinthians 1:20 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the look back below, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
You have made it to the end of 900 days. That is a remarkable thing, and God gets the glory. Whether you read every day or caught up after missing weeks, you have been through the whole Bible and the heart of the Christian faith.

This verse is a good summary of what you have read. “All the promises of God find their Yes in him.” In Genesis, God promised a seed who would crush the serpent. He promised Abraham a blessing for all nations. He promised David a son who would reign forever. He promised a new covenant, forgiveness, a new heart, his Spirit, and a new creation. Every promise, big or small, finds its Yes in Jesus Christ.

“That is why it is through him that we utter our Amen to God for his glory.” Because the promises are fulfilled in Christ, we can say “Amen,” meaning “so be it, we trust you,” to everything God says. The Bible began with God speaking and ends with the church saying “Amen.”

You do not finish the Bible; it keeps reading you. This is a place to begin, not an end. Where do you go from here? Keep reading, and read the Bible again, now that you know the story. Pick a book and read it slowly, with a study Bible or commentary. Stay rooted in a local church, where you can hear the word preached, receive the Lord’s Supper, and be loved and corrected. Pray the Psalms. Memorize Scripture. Teach someone else what you have learned. Start again at Day 1 with a friend. And hold on to Christ: he is the Yes to every promise, and he will hold on to you.
weekInReview: This final stretch of the plan took you from the fall of Babylon to the new Jerusalem. You read of the marriage supper of the Lamb, the rider on the white horse, the binding of Satan, the great white throne, the new heavens and new earth, and the last words of the Bible: “Surely I am coming soon. Amen. Come, Lord Jesus!” Psalm 72 prayed for the true King through whom all nations will be blessed, and Psalm 150 ended the Psalter with praise. Day 899 reviewed the whole of Revelation. And now you have finished the whole plan: the story of creation, fall, redemption, and new creation, told across the Old Testament, the Gospels, Acts, the letters, and Revelation, with the key doctrines of the Christian faith along the way. From Genesis 1:1 to Revelation 22:21, the Bible tells one story, whose center is Jesus Christ. God has been faithful from beginning to end.
reflectionQuestions: Looking back over the 900 days, what is one truth about God that you understand better now than when you began? How has it changed the way you pray, live, or think?
Paul says that all the promises of God find their Yes in Christ. Which promise, from anywhere in the Bible, has become most precious to you, and how do you see it fulfilled in Jesus?
What is one concrete step you will take in the next month to keep growing: a reading habit, a church community, a person to disciple or be discipled by? Write it down and tell someone.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for these 900 days in his word, naming something he has done in you.
Thank him that every promise finds its yes in Jesus.
Ask him to keep you reading, praying, and following for the rest of your life.
